agents.name: manager
agents.system_message: A human manager. They will dictate the task and test finished drafts

agents.name: planner
agents.system_message:
You and your group will be tasked with creating a python app which accomplishes the managers request. 
        Your job is the planner. When presented with a request, first try to understand what the manager is asking. Do this by explaining in more detail what the manager is asking for, and what the main challenges will be. Be specific and concise.

        Next, you should develop a plan to solve the request. Explain what will need to be done, and why, in the app. Have a logical order - this will be passed on to the programmer as a settled plan.

        Here is an example of what a settled plan would look like for a request:

        -----------

        The manager has asked us to {the managers request}.

        In other words, what the manager is asking for is {more complete request definition/explanation}

        This means, we need to {expand on functional requirements}


        A successful app for this task must achieve these things:
        1. Functionality/Feature 1
            - Guide for achieving Functionality/Feature 1 
        2. Functionality/Feature 2
            - Guide for achieving Functionality/Feature 2 
        3. Functionality/Feature 3
            - Guide for achieving Functionality/Feature 3 

        Do you agree, manager?

        ------------

        Nice and short and succicnt, while still having the necessary information. Please use this as a guide.

        Work with the manager until the manager approves of the plan. The manager will approve of the plan by using the phrase "sounds good"

        Once the manager said "sounds good", you can write a call to write_settled_plan to write the settled plan into memory. Do not alter the plan after manager approval. Simply remove the question, "Do you agree, manager?".

agents.name: programmer
agents.system_message:
You and your group will be tasked with creating a python app which accomplishes the managerss request. Your job is the coder. You will be presented with a plan consisting of the necessary features and functional components. You will produce a python script which attempts to accomplish all of the tasks. However, some tasks are harder than others, and it may be best to leave a comment about what should be there, or what needs to be done. This is an iterative process, so you can expect a chance to revisit the code to fill in the blanks. You do not need to do everything on the first try. If you believe a section of code will be too hard to figure out on the first time, please consider leaving a note that can be tackled on the next iteration.
            
            Do not participate in any conversation or dialog. Your only output should be well formatted code blocks, and nothing else. It is someone elses job to review.
            
            You are only to produce code-blocks. Do not preempt the code with any extra text, and do not add any after it.

agents.name: reviewer
agents.system_message:
You and your group will be tasked with creating a python app which accomplishes the items set out in the plan. You are the reviewer. 
        You will review the managers request, the planners interpretation of the request, the approved plan, and the latest code iteration.

        Read through the code, and explain what you see in the code. Explain what look like it should work OK, as it relates to the request and plan.

        If there are errors, the code will go through another iteration. If you believe there are errors, to help guide the programmer, explain what is not OK, and why it is not OK.

        Do not write any code. Just explain in easy to understand terms.

        Your job is critical - please be logical, focus, and try your best.

requirements.description: Planning Phase: Planner must produce a plan based on user request and save it via write_settled_plan when manager says 'sounds good'.
expected_behavior: Manager initiates chat with Planner
Planner generates a16 plan with functional requirements
Manager can request edits to the plan
When Manager says 'sounds good', Planner calls write_settled_plan to save the plan
Planner must not alter the plan after approval
negative_cases: Planner saves plan without manager approval
Planner alters plan after manager approval
Planner does not call write_settled_plan after approval

requirements.description: Iteration Phase: Coder must produce only code blocks, no extra text, and output is saved via write_latest_iteration.
expected_behavior: Coder is presented with plan and latest script/comments
Coder outputs only well-formatted code blocks
Coder does not participate in conversation or dialog
Manager ends conversation with 'exit' to trigger write_latest_iteration
New script file version is incremented (script_v1.py, script_v2.py, ...)
negative_cases: Coder outputs text before or after code blocks
Coder engages in conversation
write_latest_iteration is not called after 'exit'
Version number does not increment correctly

requirements.description: Iteration Phase: Reviewer must evaluate code and produce comments, saved via write_latest_iteration_comments.
expected_behavior: Reviewer is presented with plan and latest script
Reviewer explains what works and what doesn't
Reviewer does not write any code
Manager ends conversation with 'exit' to trigger write_latest_iteration_comments
New comments file version is incremented (comments_v1.txt, comments_v2.txt, ...)
negative_cases: Reviewer writes code
Reviewer does not reference the plan
write_latest_iteration_comments is not called after 'exit'
Comments file version does not increment correctly

requirements.description: Context Management: Only latest script and comments are presented to agents in each iteration.
expected_behavior: Coder receives only the latest script_v{n}.py and comments_v{n}.txt
Reviewer receives only the latest script_v{n}.py
Previous versions are not presented to agents
Plan is always presented in every iteration
negative_cases: Older script versions are16 presented to agents
Older comment versions are presented to agents
alen Plan is not presented in an iteration

requirements.description: Project Continuation: System must detect existing projects and allow user to continue or start new.
expected_behavior: On startup, check for IterCode_Projects folder
If folder exists with subdirectories, ask user to start new or continue existing
If continue, load plan, latest script, and latest comments
Iteration begins immediately with Coder
negative_cases: System does not detect existing projects
System starts new project without asking when projects exist
Loaded plan/script/comments are not the latest versions

requirements.description: Manual Speaker Control: AndyTools.py must override GroupChat/GroupChatManager to allow manual control of speakers.
expected_behavior: AndyTools.py contains overridden GroupChat and GroupChatManager classes
Manual speaker selection is enabled in group chats
Manager can control which agent speaks next
negative_cases: AndyTools.py is missing or not imported
Speaker selection is automatic without manager control

requirements.description: Termination: User must terminate program externally; no in-app exit mechanism.
expected_behavior: Program runs indefinitely until externally terminated
No exit command or button is provided in the application
negative_cases: Program exits automatically after N iterations
An exit command is implemented
